analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (19.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 23bps to 7323 (+7% YTD), its fifth straight down day. Retailers had a top-5 session YTD (TJX +8%). GS describes conviction as low and trading activity as top down, and prime brokerage data show elevated selling across Tech.
Levels cited: US 10yr yield 5.05%, Brent $92, Gold $3740, Bitcoin $63k. Copper fell 5% the previous day, which GS ties to the AI trade. GS says all eyes are on IPO trading.

FOMC minutes: a couple of participants said a hike larger than 25bp could warrant consideration at the next meeting if incoming inflation data were unfavorable. GS expects two more 25bp hikes, in Dec26 and Mar27.

Palo Alto rose 8% after hours on strong numbers and better margin. Revenue growth guidance was raised to 26.5-26.9% y/y against consensus of 23.4%, and management has more visibility into budget dynamics. GS rates it Buy and raised its 12m price target to $440 from $390.

Palo Alto agreed to acquire Applied Compute for an EV of $4.5bn, all stock. Applied Compute is a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight AI models. GS says the deal gives Palo Alto several levers to attach to token consumption, such as software firewalls.
Palo Alto call quotes: agentic traffic is up about 9x y/y, and management expects industry token revenue to pass $1 trillion by 2029.
TJX said it has not seen a dramatic shift in its sales trend by income group.

GTA VI has just launched, 13 years after GTA V. GS flags $1bn as the number to watch this weekend, the retail sales GTA V generated in its first 3 days. Pre-order demand exceeded previous franchise benchmarks. GS notes the 'GTA flu' is ongoing.

GS asset allocation: modestly pro-risk. Slowing growth against rates relief should drive risk appetite in 2027. Slowing earnings growth and higher volatility imply lower risk-adjusted returns. GS favors selective growth alongside quality, defensive and high dividend/buyback stocks, and says bonds should offer a better buffer against equity weakness as nominal growth peaks.

GS prefers equities to credit. Tight spreads, releveraging and rising issuance limit credit returns, while equities have more upside under favorable earnings and AI scenarios. GS cites the late-1990s as precedent for equities rising with greater volatility while credit lags.
Google announced smart glasses with a camera, microphone, speaker and AI assistant but no display, following Meta.
CTA positioning in US equities is short almost $10bn, the lowest since April. For the first time in weeks, flows from the cohort are skewed to the upside.

GS forecasts the S&P 500 at 8700 in 2027, up 17%, against a 21% annualized return over the past 4 years. EPS growth is expected to slow from about 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. P/E fell 19% in 2026 and sits near its 10-year average, and GS's base case holds it near 18x.
Microsoft's CEO, discussing a 60k layoff, said software engineering is not going away but the team structure and the engineer's work have a new operating point.

Nvidia CFO comments: demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers, Rubin is already meaningful, compute remains fully utilized, and cash generation is enormous. An extra week in 4Q26 flatters sequential growth. China is optional upside to the guide, memory is a major strategic constraint, and power and financing are becoming as important as chips.
Druckenmiller said he cannot remember a period with less clarity on where markets will be in 12 months.
The S&P 500 has returned 120% (21% p.a.) since the late-2022 bull market start, the strongest 4-year return in 50 years outside the Dot-Com Bubble and post-recession recoveries.
US-listed equity ETFs took in $59.3bn last week against $55.2bn the week before, beating 91% of the 46 weeks this year.
